given: An image file img.png that is 300 wide x 200 high. Exactly one class has segments on this image: class id 2, whose alias is 'dog.animal'; therefore class_order = [2] (sorted unique class ids of the image's segments, legacy/lazylabel/src/lazylabel/core/segment_manager.py:87-95). One segment of class 2 whose FINAL mask - after pixel priority and after any active crop - covers exactly the 100 mask pixels x = 100..109 and y = 50..59 inclusive. State this as pixel extents, not as polygon corners: a polygon drawn with corners (100,50)-(110,60) rasterizes to 11x11 = 121 pixels, because cv2.fillPoly includes both edge rows/columns (segment_manager.py:182-184), and would instead yield bbox [100,50,11,11], area 100 and segmentation [100,50,100,60,110,60,110,50]. COCO JSON is among the selected export formats, so per-object contours are built (legacy/lazylabel/src/lazylabel/core/exporters/__init__.py:86-94; legacy/lazylabel/src/lazylabel/ui/managers/save_export_manager.py:445-452).
when: The user saves the image's annotations and the COCO exporter runs (CocoExporter.export, legacy/lazylabel/src/lazylabel/core/exporters/coco.py:40-97). It walks every object contour yielded by iter_object_contours (exporters/__init__.py:114-136) and writes one file, <image basename without extension> + '_coco.json' (coco.py:99-100), next to the image.
then: img_coco.json is written containing exactly this object, with top-level keys in this order - 'images', 'annotations', 'categories' (coco.py:87-91): images = [ { "id": 1, "file_name": "img.png", "width": 300, "height": 200 } ] (coco.py:53-54; file_name is the basename only, width/height are the FULL image size); annotations = [ { "id": 1, "image_id": 1, "category_id": 2, "bbox": [100, 50, 10, 10], "area": 81, "segmentation": [[100, 50, 100, 59, 109, 59, 109, 50]], "iscrowd": 0 } ] (coco.py:67-81; field order as written); categories = [ { "id": 2, "name": "dog", "supercategory": "animal" } ] (coco.py:44-50). Verified by re-running cv2.boundingRect, cv2.contourArea and cv2.findContours(RETR_EXTERNAL, CHAIN_APPROX_SIMPLE) on this exact mask with OpenCV 4.12.0 / numpy 2.2.6 from the app venv: contour has 4 points, boundingRect = (100,50,10,10), contourArea = 81.0 -> int -> 81. Note area 81, NOT the 100 mask pixels: the contour runs through pixel CENTRES, so area is about (w-1)*(h-1) for a rectangle.
and:
The serialization is part of the contract because exports must stay byte-identical. The body is json.dump(coco_data, f, indent=2) (coco.py:96): 2-space indent, every array element on its own line, key separator ': ', item separator ',' with no trailing space, and NO trailing newline at end of file. ensure_ascii defaults to True, so any non-ASCII character in a class name or file name is escaped as \uXXXX (verified: 'cafe' with an e-acute is written as café, never as raw UTF-8) - JavaScript's JSON.stringify does NOT do this and must be post-processed. The file is opened in text mode, open(path, 'w') (coco.py:95), so on Windows every '
' is translated to '
' (verified: the written file contained 17 CR and 17 LF); on Linux/macOS it stays '
'. The parent directory is created if missing (coco.py:94). If and only if there are zero annotations, no file is written and export() returns None (coco.py:84-85) - and nothing is deleted, so a stale _coco.json from an earlier save survives on disk and can still be read back (export_all never deletes, exporters/__init__.py:189-206). Deletion of annotation files happens only when the segment list is empty (save_export_manager.py:106-109; ui/main_window.py:6589-6594).
parameters: category_id = ctx.class_order[channel], i.e. the raw LazyLabel class id with no +1 background shift, so class 0 is written as category id 0 (coco.py:71; channel is the index into class_order, segment_manager.py:276, 283). category id = the same class id (coco.py:49). Category name/supercategory = the class alias split at the LAST '.' via rsplit('.', 1) (coco.py:19-27); with no dot, supercategory equals name (coco.py:27); with no alias at all the value is str(class_id), used for BOTH name and supercategory (coco.py:46). Categories are emitted for every id in class_order, in ascending class-id order, even for a class that ends up with zero annotations; classes that have no segment on this image get no category (coco.py:44-50). image id = 1, hardcoded (coco.py:54, 70). Annotation ids are 1, 2, 3 ... assigned in iteration order and restarting at 1 on every export call (coco.py:58, 82). bbox = [x, y, w, h] from cv2.boundingRect, all ints, edge-inclusive so w = maxX - minX + 1 (coco.py:65, 72). area = TRUNCATE-toward-zero of cv2.contourArea(contour) when the contour has 3 or more POINTS, else int(w) * int(h) of the bounding box (coco.py:73-77). The truncation is load-bearing: Python int() drops the fraction, it does not round - verified 24.5 -> 24 (8x8 lower triangle) and 0.5 -> 0 (1-pixel-wide L). In TypeScript use Math.trunc (equivalently Math.floor, since contourArea is never negative); Math.round would diverge on the many real masks whose area ends in .5. iscrowd = 0 always (coco.py:79). segmentation = [polygon], a list containing exactly ONE flat [x1,y1,x2,y2,...] integer array (coco.py:62, 78). Polygon vertices come from contour_to_polygon (exporters/__init__.py:139-157) and are NOT simplified - unlike YOLO Segmentation, which applies cv2.approxPolyDP with epsilon = 0.001 * arcLength (legacy/lazylabel/src/lazylabel/core/exporters/yolo_segmentation.py:33-36). Contours are cv2.findContours(mask, RETR_EXTERNAL, CHAIN_APPROX_SIMPLE) - outer boundaries only, corner points only, in OpenCV's own order (segment_manager.py:303-305; exporters/__init__.py:132-134). Output suffix = os.path.splitext(image_path)[0] + '_coco.json' (coco.py:99-100).
edgeCases: Area under-counts pixels: the polygon runs through pixel centres, so the 100-pixel 10x10 block yields area 81, roughly (w-1)*(h-1). COCO's small/medium/large buckets (32^2, 96^2) in pycocotools will bucket objects differently than a pixel-count area would.

Area is truncated, not rounded (coco.py:74). An 8x8 lower-triangle mask gives contourArea 24.5 -> 24; a 1-pixel-wide L shape gives 0.5 -> 0. A contour with >= 3 points uses the contour area even when that area is 0 - it does NOT fall back to the bounding box.

The >= 3 test counts contour POINTS, not pixels (coco.py:75). A 1-pixel object gives a 1-point contour -> area = 1*1 = 1. A 10-pixel horizontal line gives a 2-point contour -> area = 10*1 = 10. A 10-pixel DIAGONAL line also gives a 2-point contour -> area = 10*10 = 100 for 10 pixels of ink (a 5-pixel diagonal gives 25).

Contours of 1 or 2 points are padded to a closed 4-point ring rather than dropped (exporters/__init__.py:148-157), so segmentation always holds at least 8 numbers: a single pixel at (100,50) becomes [100,50,100,50,100,50,100,50]; a 10-pixel line becomes [100,50,109,50,109,50,100,50].
Only OUTER contours are kept (RETR_EXTERNAL), so holes are silently filled: a 20x20 ring with a 10x10 hole holds 300 pixels but exports one annotation with bbox [100,50,20,20] and area 361.

One segment can produce SEVERAL annotations. A segment split into two blobs yields one annotation per blob, all sharing the same category_id (exporters/__init__.py:122-126; segment_manager.py:303-313).

Annotation order is segment order, then OpenCV's contour order within a segment - it is not spatial and not sorted. Verified: for one mask with blobs at (5,5) and (30,30), OpenCV 4.12 returned (30,30) FIRST, so it gets annotation id 1. Do not assume top-left-first ordering.

An alias with an unintended dot splits wrongly: 'St. Bernard' -> name 'St', supercategory ' Bernard' (leading space preserved); 'v1.0' -> name 'v1', supercategory '0'; 'a.b.c' -> name 'a.b', supercategory 'c' (last dot wins); 'dog.' -> supercategory ''; '.dog' -> name ''.
A class with no alias writes str(class_id) into BOTH name and supercategory, e.g. class 5 -> {"id": 5, "name": "5", "supercategory": "5"} (coco.py:46).

Alias round-trip is lossy. The loader rebuilds the alias as name + '.' + supercategory only when supercategory != name (legacy/lazylabel/src/lazylabel/core/file_manager.py:635-637), so an alias of 'x.x' is written as name 'x' / supercategory 'x' and reloads as plain 'x'.

A category is still written for a class whose every pixel was removed by an active crop or by pixel priority; that class then has a category and no annotation (coco.py:44-50 runs independently of the annotation loop).

Coordinates, width and height are always in FULL-image space, even with an active crop: cropping blanks the pixels outside the crop rather than cutting the image down (file_manager.py:712-739). The multi-view save path never applies a crop at all (main_window.py:6615-6631 passes no crop_coords).

Stale-file hazard: if segments exist but all of them are cropped away, zero annotations are produced, so the exporter writes nothing (coco.py:84-85) yet deletes nothing (exporters/__init__.py:189-206) - an out-of-date _coco.json stays on disk and is still eligible to be loaded back, since COCO_JSON is third in LOAD_PRIORITY (exporters/__init__.py:73-81).

Per-image ids collide when files are merged into one dataset: image_id is always 1 and annotation ids always restart at 1. LazyLabel's own loader ignores id, image_id, area, iscrowd and the whole images block, reading only categories and each annotation's category_id / segmentation / bbox (file_manager.py:626-690), so these fields are never validated on the way back in.
Polygon is NOT simplified, unlike YOLO Segmentation (coco.py:62 vs yolo_segmentation.py:33-36); the vertices are exactly OpenCV's CHAIN_APPROX_SIMPLE corner points, not every boundary pixel.

Structural fallback: iter_object_contours only uses per-object contours when ctx.instances is non-empty (exporters/__init__.py:122). If an empty instances list ever reaches the exporter, it contours the MERGED per-class mask channels instead (exporters/__init__.py:128-136), which fuses touching or overlapping same-class objects into one annotation. A port must reproduce both branches.
answer: The open question - should COCO 'area' be the mask pixel count instead of the contour polygon area - is answered NO by the approved decision that exports stay byte-identical to legacy output: the Node/TypeScript port must keep area = trunc(contourArea(contour)) for contours of 3+ points and w*h otherwise (coco.py:73-77), which yields 81 for the 100-pixel 10x10 block. The suspectedDefect is real and stays as a documented deviation from the pycocotools convention (it shifts small/medium/large metric buckets), not as something to fix; if the product owner later wants true pixel-count area it is a versioned format change, not a port bug. Verifying the card clause by clause, every number in it is correct - I re-ran the OpenCV calls in-memory with OpenCV 4.12.0 from the app venv and got contour [100,50,100,59,109,59,109,50], boundingRect (100,50,10,10) and contourArea 81.0 - but the card was wrong or incomplete in seven ways. (1) The Given was ambiguous: it must mean mask pixels x=100..109, y=50..59, because a polygon with corners (100,50)-(110,60) fills 11x11 via cv2.fillPoly (segment_manager.py:182-184) and would give bbox [100,50,11,11] and area 100. (2) 'area = int(...)' is too weak for a TS implementer: Python int() TRUNCATES (coco.py:74) - 24.5 -> 24, 0.5 -> 0 - so Math.round would silently diverge on real masks even though it passes the card's example. (3) The >= 3 test counts contour POINTS, not pixels (coco.py:75), and the card never gave the sub-3-point fallback numbers (single pixel -> 1, 10-pixel line -> 10, 10-pixel diagonal -> 100) nor the 1-/2-point padding to a 4-point ring (exporters/__init__.py:148-157). (4) 'One annotation per object' actually means one per OUTER contour (RETR_EXTERNAL, segment_manager.py:303-305): holes are filled (a 20x20 ring with a 10x10 hole = 300 pixels but area 361) and a multi-blob segment produces several annotations sharing one category_id (exporters/__init__.py:122-126). (5) The card omitted the whole categories rule - every id in class_order in ascending order (segment_manager.py:87-95), emitted even with zero annotations, raw class id with no +1 background shift so class 0 is category 0, and str(class_id) for both name and supercategory when there is no alias (coco.py:44-50). (6) 'No file when there are no objects' was misleading: nothing is written (coco.py:84-85) AND nothing is deleted (exporters/__init__.py:189-206), so a stale _coco.json survives and stays loadable at LOAD_PRIORITY rank 3 (exporters/__init__.py:73-81); files are deleted only when the segment list is empty (save_export_manager.py:106-109), which matches the approved decision that annotation files are deleted only on explicit user action. (7) The card said nothing about serialization, which the byte-identical decision makes contractual: json.dump(indent=2) with fixed key order images/annotations/categories, ensure_ascii=True so non-ASCII is escaped as \uXXXX (JSON.stringify does not), and text-mode write (coco.py:95) that emits CRLF on Windows and LF elsewhere, with no trailing newline. The three things an implementer must watch hardest are the truncation, the ensure_ascii escaping, and the annotation ORDER - OpenCV's contour order is not spatial, and in 4.12 a blob at (30,30) came back before one at (5,5), so ids 1..N cannot be assigned by sorting.
corrections: Given: disambiguated to explicit pixel extents (x 100-109, y 50-59) and added the 11x11 counter-example for polygon-corner input; added image size, class_order = [2] and the fact that COCO selection is what populates per-object contours

Then: replaced the two fragments with the complete file body in written key order (images/annotations/categories), including file_name basename and full-image width/height, and recorded that the numbers were re-verified against OpenCV 4.12.0

And: was null; now carries the serialization and file-lifecycle contract (indent=2, key/field order, ensure_ascii \uXXXX escaping, CRLF on Windows vs LF elsewhere, no trailing newline, directory creation, write-nothing-delete-nothing on zero annotations)
Parameters: area restated as TRUNCATE toward zero (Math.trunc/Math.floor), not 'int()', with the 24.5 -> 24 and 0.5 -> 0 evidence and an explicit warning against Math.round
Parameters: clarified that the >= 3 threshold counts contour POINTS and that a 3+-point contour uses contour area even when it is 0

Parameters: added the full categories rule - ascending class_order ids, raw class id with no +1 shift (class 0 -> category 0), emitted even with zero annotations, str(class_id) for both fields when no alias, supercategory = name when the alias has no dot
Parameters: added that bbox is edge-inclusive (w = maxX - minX + 1) and that segmentation is a list containing exactly one flat array
Parameters: added the contour source (RETR_EXTERNAL, CHAIN_APPROX_SIMPLE) and the explicit contrast with YOLO Segmentation's approxPolyDP epsilon = 0.001 * arcLength
Parameters: removed the duplicated 'annotation ids restart at 1 per file' / 'annotation ids start at 1 per file' clause
Edge cases: added area truncation, the sub-3-point fallback numbers (1 / 10 / 100 for pixel, line, diagonal), and the 1-/2-point padding to a 4-point ring
Edge cases: added holes-are-filled (ring: 300 pixels, area 361) and one-segment-many-annotations
Edge cases: added annotation ORDER - segment order then OpenCV contour order, with the verified (30,30)-before-(5,5) example
Edge cases: added the no-alias case (str(class_id) in both fields) and extended the alias-split cases with 'a.b.c', 'dog.' and '.dog'
Edge cases: added the lossy alias round-trip ('x.x' reloads as 'x', file_manager.py:635-637)
Edge cases: added category-without-annotation when crop or pixel priority removes every pixel of a class
Edge cases: added full-image coordinate space under crop, and that the multi-view save path applies no crop at all
Edge cases: rewrote 'No file when there are no objects' as the stale-file hazard - writes nothing, deletes nothing, old file stays loadable at LOAD_PRIORITY rank 3
Edge cases: expanded the id-collision note to record that the loader ignores id, image_id, area, iscrowd and the images block entirely
Edge cases: added the empty-instances fallback branch, which contours merged per-class channels and fuses same-class objects
unresolved: Two items need a product-owner call, neither blocking the port. (1) The byte-identical target is platform-dependent: coco.py:95 writes in text mode, so the legacy bytes carry CRLF on Windows and LF on Linux/macOS. The equivalence harness must name which platform's output is the reference, or normalize line endings before comparing - otherwise a correct Node port fails on one OS and passes on the other. (2) The stale-file hazard (segments exist but all are cropped away: nothing written, nothing deleted, an out-of-date _coco.json stays loadable at LOAD_PRIORITY rank 3) is legacy behaviour that the approved 'delete only on explicit user action' decision preserves as-is. Whether that is acceptable, or should be surfaced as a warning in the rewrite, is a product decision and deserves its own rule card - it is a data-integrity gap, not a formatting one.
